title: Pathogens and antigens
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:35Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-01T14:55:57Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No bank point teaches antigens marking cells as self or non-self or allergens triggering responses; the closest card, Types of pathogens, covers only the classes of pathogen, so it is broader and does not match the new point.

draft.title: Pathogens and antigens
card: a molecule, often a protein, that the immune system can recognise. Your own cells carry self antigens. Foreign cells and viruses carry non-self antigens.
a disease-causing organism made of cells, such as a bacterium, fungus or protist.
a disease-causing agent with no cell structure, such as a virus or a prion. A virus must use a host cell to reproduce.
a harmless substance, such as pollen, that triggers an immune response in some people. It acts as an antigen, even though it is not a pathogen.
draft.remember: Antigens tell the immune system self from non-self. Pathogens cause disease, and allergens set off a response without being pathogens.

a.q: What does the immune system use antigens for?
opts: To recognise cells and particles as self or non-self
To destroy any cell that carries a protein on its surface
To make a cell divide when it is infected by a virus
To carry oxygen to cells that are under attack
a.why: Antigens are molecules that the immune system can recognise, so they mark a cell as self or non-self. Having a protein on the surface does not mean a cell is destroyed, because all your own cells carry self antigens.
a.clue: Think about how the body tells its own cells from foreign ones.

b.q: Sam sneezes and has itchy eyes near flowering grass. The immune system is responding to grass pollen. Which statement is correct?
opts: Pollen is an allergen, and it is not a pathogen
Pollen is a cellular pathogen, because it comes from a plant
Pollen is a non-cellular pathogen, like a virus
Pollen is a self antigen, so it should not cause a response
b.why: Pollen is a harmless substance that triggers an immune response in some people, which makes it an allergen. It does not cause infectious disease, so it is not a pathogen of either type. Coming from a plant does not make it a cellular pathogen.
b.clue: Does pollen cause an infection, or only trigger a response?

a.best: To recognise cells and particles as self or non-self

b.best: Pollen is an allergen, and it is not a pathogen
